subject: ACME - competitive bake-off plan and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-22T17:05:00Z
Subject: ACME - competitive bake-off plan and next steps

Thanks for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call:
- Objectives: validate inference latency/cost for ACME's realtime assistant (1k concurrent sessions, 95th latency target <200ms per request) and verify private VPC deployment for PHI data.
- Primary comparisons: Redwood Dedicated vs AWS Bedrock endpoints vs GCP Vertex AI (inference) — focus on tail latency, cost per 1M tokens, and failover behavior.
- Must-haves: model version pinning, KV cache support, function/tool calling, audit logs, and SOC2 evidence.

Proposed bake-off plan (attached spreadsheet):
1) Baseline tests (3 days): run 50k requests across each vendor at ACME traffic profile
2) Throughput/latency (2 days): sustained load to observe 95th and p99
3) Cost run (1 day): estimate unit cost at production scale
4) Regression/quality (2 days): run 200 prompt blackbox evals
Success criteria:
- 95th latency <=200ms for 90% of traffic, p99 within 2x target
- End-to-end cost advantage or parity within 15% vs hyperscalers
- No functional regressions on prompt set
Owners and asks:
- Redwood infra owner: Rishi Malhotra (provision test env, provide creds)
- Redwood sales lead: Aditya Rao (orchestrate plan, coordinate logs/analytics)
- Pricing/contact for procurement: Lauren Bishop (pricing and terms)

Can you confirm the test window next week (Mar 24 - Mar 30) and the ACME technical contact who will share test data and prompt sets? Attaching plan and SOW draft for reference.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-bakeoff-test-plan.xlsx, acme-sow-draft.pdf

From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-03-22T20:30:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME - competitive bake-off plan and next steps

Thanks Aditya — great recap. We are aligned on objectives and the proposed scope. A few clarifications from our side: 
- Procurement will need a cost estimate (per 1M tokens) and any standard SLA language you provide before we lock the SOW.
- Technical contact for the tests will be Devindra Singh (devindra.singh@acme.com). He will share the prompt set and a sanitized subset of PII data for the privacy test.
- For the test accounts: can you provision a short-lived dedicated environment or temporary API keys scoped to the bake-off? We prefer isolated endpoints rather than shared hosted endpoints.

If you can confirm provisioning steps and a simple checklist for our infra team, we can confirm the March 24 - 30 window.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Hayes
Senior Product Manager | ACME Inc.
procurement@acme.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-03-22T21:10:00Z
Subject: Fwd: ACME - competitive bake-off plan and next steps (internal owners)

Looping you both in to provision and price this bake-off. Jordan confirmed Devindra Singh as ACME's technical contact and prefers an isolated environment. Key asks below (from original):
- Provision: short-lived dedicated test environment (VPC) or temp API keys scoped to the ACME test. We should also provide a short runbook for onboarding.
- Capacity: allocate the equivalent of 2 x A100/4 GPU capacity for the baseline runs and a path to scale up for throughput runs.
- Metrics: collect token-level cost, per-request latency (p50/p95/p99), and model version pinning behavior.
- Deliverables: aggregated latency/cost dashboard, request traces for any failures, and a summary report.

Proposed owners and timeline:
- Infra/provisioning: Rishi (target: provision by EOD Mar 23)
- Pricing/SOW: Lauren (deliver draft pricing and SLA language by EOD Mar 23)
- Redwood test execution support: Aditya (coordinate logs and evals during Mar 24 - 30)

Can you confirm you can meet those dates? I attached the plan and SOW draft to the original email.

Regards,
Aditya

From: Jordan Hayes <jordan.hayes@acme.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Devindra Singh <devindra.singh@acme.com>, procurement@acme.com
Date: 2026-03-23T15:00:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME - competitive bake-off plan and next steps

Thanks team — confirmed. We can commit to Mar 24 - 30. Devindra will share a sanitized prompt set by end of day tomorrow. Procurement still needs the pricing estimate but said the SOW review can happen in parallel. For the environment: temporary API keys are fine as long as they are isolated and we have short-lived credentials to revoke.

Devindra (cc'd) — can you please confirm the prompt set and whether you need any specific test harness (JMeter, k6, custom script)?

Jordan

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-23T16:20:00Z
Subject: Re: ACME - competitive bake-off plan and next steps (infra ready)

Confirming infra provisioning. I will: 
- Stand up a short-lived VPC-scoped test env and issue scoped API keys (redwood-test-credentials.txt attached).
- Pre-configure model variants and KV cache layers to match ACME's profile.
- Hook token-level cost reporting and latency tracing to the shared Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdEfGhIjKlmNopQ

ETA: test env and creds available by 2026-03-23T20:00:00Z. Lauren, once you share pricing, I will add cost hooks so we can produce an apples-to-apples cost comparison.

Rishi Malhotra
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-test-credentials.txt
